features.behavior: Local-server authentication and browser hardening, landing FIRST in plan 0006 because it protects even the read-only product and is a precondition for any mutating route: the CLI mints a cryptographically random per-session token at startup, the served UI receives it (injected into index.html or fetched via a one-time bootstrap), and every /api route rejects requests without it (401, structured error) - closing the current no-auth surface where any local process/user can call the full API and where cross-origin CSRF is blocked only implicitly by Fastify's JSON content-type requirement (pgweb/DbGate precedent for local web DB tools). Security headers land with it: CSP on the served SPA (also neutralizes DB-data-driven request exfil via F086's image URL previews), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options. Open decision (exec plan 0006 #3): header-based token + fetch/blob downloads vs cookie - the CSV export links (plain <a href>) must keep working, so the choice must cover download URLs. E2E: UI works end-to-end with the token; a tokenless curl to every /api route 401s; docs/SECURITY.md updated. No dependency on other plan slices.

features.behavior: Batched schema introspection, landing BEFORE per-engine permission work multiplies the current fan-out: GET /api/tables today calls getTable per table - each >= 4 catalog queries plus a row-count estimate (with a possible exact COUNT(*) fallback) - through an unbounded Promise.all (packages/server/src/routes/tables.ts), which hammers large databases and was already tracked as tech debt. Adapters gain a batched all-tables metadata path (e.g. getAllTables(): one/few set-based catalog queries per engine - information_schema joins on Postgres/MySQL, sqlite_master + per-table pragmas with bounded concurrency on SQLite, listCollections + capped sampling on MongoDB); the route uses it; getTable stays for single-table use. Row-count estimates become part of the batched query (pg_class.reltuples, information_schema.TABLES.TABLE_ROWS) rather than per-table round trips. Conformance asserts the batched path returns the same shape as N x getTable on every engine. F092-F095 attach per-table permissions to this batched path. Depends on F091.

features.evidence: PR #98 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/98), pushed as 183cb3a. DatabaseAdapter gains getAllTables(): TableMetadata[] in the same shape N getTable() calls would produce. Postgres/MySQL each get one batched query for columns, PK/FK, and indexes across every table (information_schema, no per-table filter); row counts batch too - Postgres keeps getTable()'s reltuples-estimate-with-exact-fallback semantics exactly (one estimate query, then a targeted exact COUNT(*) only for never-ANALYZEd tables), MySQL uses a single UNION ALL of exact COUNT(*) per table rather than the originally-suggested information_schema.TABLES.TABLE_ROWS estimate, since that can lag right after insert and would break exact parity with getTable() (a documented engineering deviation from the feature's literal text, made for correctness/determinism). SQLite/MongoDB have no cross-table catalog query for either engine (pragmas and field-sampling are inherently per-table/collection) - the batching win there is moving the fan-out from the route's unbounded Promise.all into a bounded sequential loop inside the adapter that reuses getTable(), correct by construction. GET /api/tables (packages/server/src/routes/tables.ts) now calls getAllTables() directly instead of getOverview() + Promise.all(getTable). A @qyre/testing-conformance case asserts the batched path returns the exact same shape as calling getTable() per table, live against all 4 engines. Verified: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (84 passed), pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test (48 passed, incl. the new parity test), each adapter's own test suite unchanged, pnpm check:quiet, pnpm verify:pr (full local gate incl. @full E2E against live Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB - Schema tab exercises getAllTables() end-to-end). The UI shows a subtle kind badge in the sidebar/schema views; every later mutation/DDL surface gates on kind (editing a view's rows, DROP TABLE on a view, truncating a matview are all prevented up front with the reason stated). Read-only behavior otherwise unchanged. Conformance: a fixture view per SQL engine (and a MongoDB view) reports its kind correctly everywhere. Depends on F123.

features.evidence: PR #99 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/99), pushed as 2ac72f1. TableMetadata gains a required kind: 'table' | 'view' | 'materialized-view' | 'collection'. features.evidence: PR #103 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/103), pushed as 1b8b286. Deviates from the plan's literal ROLE_TABLE_GRANTS/ROLE_SCHEMA_GRANTS approach after live verification against MySQL 8.4.10: information_schema.ROLE_SCHEMA_GRANTS does not exist, and ROLE_TABLE_GRANTS only sees exact-table role grants (misses schema-wide db.* role grants entirely). Instead, packages/drivers/mysql/src/permissions.ts parses the session's own SHOW GRANTS output, which MySQL resolves into the merged effective grant set including active default roles - no MySQL-version gate needed since SHOW GRANTS resolving default roles is standard from MySQL 8.0.0. Extracted packages/drivers/mysql/src/catalog.ts (SYSTEM_SCHEMAS/tableKey) mirroring Postgres's module structure. getCapabilities() reports real session writability from @@global.read_only/@@session.transaction_read_only plus parsed grants; getTable and the batched F123 getAllTables() path attach per-table TablePermissions via tablePermissionsFromGrants (direct table grant, schema-wide db.* grant, or role-derived grant - all resolved identically since SHOW GRANTS already merges them). features.evidence: PR #104 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/104), pushed as 82f4bd4. Deviates from the plan's literal text in the same spirit as F093's SHOW GRANTS pivot: adapter.ts's connect() previously force-opened every SQLite connection with { readonly: true } unconditionally, as Qyre's own defense-in-depth policy independent of the underlying file's real permissions - under that policy db.readonly always read true, making the 'opened with a read-only flag' gate a permanent constant and the whole capabilities feature a no-op. connect() now opens normally (falling back to an explicit read-only open only if that throws outright), so db.readonly becomes a real, live signal. To keep the safety guarantee at least as strong as before, runReadOnlyQuery's authoritative backstop moved from the connection being permanently opened read-only to toggling PRAGMA query_only around each query (try/finally) - the same query-time enforcement pattern Postgres/MySQL already use via runInReadOnlyTransaction. New packages/drivers/sqlite/src/capabilities.ts (computeCapabilities/tablePermissionsFromCapabilities) gates writability on four independent, live-verified signals: file OS-writability, containing-directory OS-writability (WAL/rollback-journal sidecar files need directory write even when the file itself is writable - verified live that a writable file in a read-only directory still refuses every write), PRAGMA query_only, and the connection's own open mode. Per-table TablePermissions are uniform per file and derived directly from the session-level result, computed once and shared across getAllTables()'s batched (F123) path. readOnlyReason for a non-writable SQLite session is now 'connection' (replacing the F091 stub's 'grants', which was never accurate for an engine with no grants concept). 7 new unit tests in tests/capabilities.test.ts against real temp files/directories (writable, chmod-read-only file, read-only directory, an explicitly readonly-opened 'mode=ro' connection - better-sqlite3 has no URI-string mode=ro support, confirmed by reading its C++ source, so the boolean readonly option is the literal implementation of that concept here) plus 3 new/updated integration tests, including a direct-bypass proof of the new query_only backstop mirroring Postgres/MySQL's own such tests. testing-conformance's capabilities test gained a dedicated sqlite branch (its self-contained fixture is a normal writable tempdir file, so it now expects full writability like Postgres/MySQL, except supportsDatabaseManagement: false). features.evidence: PR #105 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/105), pushed as b6b5e4f. getCapabilities()/per-collection TablePermissions derive from db.runCommand({connectionStatus:1, showPrivileges:true}) as specified, mapping find (select) and insert/update/remove (row mutations) plus createCollection/dropCollection (supportsDdl) and createIndex/dropIndex (supportsIndexManagement) per resource - exact db+collection, db-level wildcard (collection:''), cross-db wildcard (db:''), and anyResource:true, all shapes live-verified against a real mongod by creating read/readWrite/dbAdmin/custom-anyResource users and capturing their exact connectionStatus output as unit-test fixture data. System databases (admin/local/config) and system.* collections are excluded from the session-level aggregate checks, matching introspectSchemas' existing listing filter (now shared via a new catalog.ts, mirroring the other three adapters' module split). An unauthenticated connection (empty authenticatedUsers) is treated as full access, live-verified as mongod's actual default when authorization isn't enabled. supportsDatabaseManagement and supportsTransactions are always false for this slice (deviation, documented in permissions.ts's top comment): MongoDB has no paired create/drop-database privilege, and real multi-document transactions additionally require replica-set topology a standalone mongod can't provide regardless of grants - both out of scope for a privilege-only introspection slice. Introspection failure degrades to read-only, logged. Scoping decision confirmed with the user before implementing: rather than the plan's literal 'adds a restricted fixture user to the mongo init', testing a genuinely restricted user live would require enabling MongoDB authorization globally on the shared docker-compose/CI container, breaking every existing anonymous Mongo test/fixture/e2e spec - a disproportionate blast radius versus F092-F094's purely additive restricted fixtures. Restricted-access scenarios are instead covered by 10 unit tests against the live-verified connectionStatus shapes; the live integration test proves the unauthenticated-full-access path end-to-end against the real, unchanged container. A pre-existing MongoDB-only safety test (scanning adapter source for accidental write-API calls) needed scoping to exclude permissions.ts, which legitimately contains MongoDB's own privilege action-name vocabulary (createCollection/createIndex/etc.) as string literals, not method calls - added a second, stricter test that only flags actual `methodName(` call syntax in that file.
